description: Adversarial gloss set for TODO.md 2.2: does the model verification pass notice that an item's English gloss is WRONG? 36 matched pairs drawn from the owner's own last corpus pilot (data/corpus_pilot_review.jsonl, 430 accepted items). Each pair contributes two rows: one 'wrong' row carrying a hand-authored defective gloss, and one 'correct' row carrying the item's own real gloss unchanged. 72 rows, 36 wrong and 36 correct, six defect kinds at six pairs each: wrong_tense, wrong_person, wrong_number, wrong_definiteness, wrong_polarity, unrelated. Every German prompt, answer, cue and correct gloss is copied verbatim from that pilot file; only the wrong glosses are authored.
instructions: Golden fixture (CLAUDE.md section 7): versioned, not regenerated casually. Append new pairs rather than editing existing ones, and bump 'version' in the commit that does it. The matched design is the point: a pair's two rows differ in the gloss and in nothing else, so a rejection on the wrong row that does not also happen on the correct row is attributable to the gloss. Run the two arms in SEPARATE verification calls so the model never sees a pair's two glosses side by side. Loaded by scripts/eval_gloss_adversarial.py.
source: data/corpus_pilot_review.jsonl, pilot batch corpus_pilot_7902699b, 430 accepted items, hand-audited at 10 defects (2.3%).
